papers.title_in_file: A Review of Design Concerns in Superconducting Quantum Circuits
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2411.16967v5 (30 May 2025); the file name says 2024.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section VII (closing the design loop) and Section VIII Outlook; the middle technical sections were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A short review of how a superconducting quantum circuit device is designed, from circuit graph and layout to electromagnetic simulation and measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper is a short review of the process of designing a superconducting circuit device for quantum information applications, and that it acts as a starter document for researchers.
quotes: In this short review we describe the process of designing a superconducting circuit device for quantum information applications.
acts as a starter document for researchers working on any of these challenges.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope, Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the most common reason for device parameters that miss their design targets is an inaccurate electromagnetic simulation of the device or an inaccurate translation of the simulation results to a Hamiltonian, and that the usual approach to a disagreement is empirical.
quotes: The most common reason for these missed parameters is an inaccurate electromagnetic simulation of the device and/or an inaccurate translation of simulation results to Hamiltonian.

Again the usual approach is empirical: if experimental results disagree with simulation, designers run larger simulations with tighter tolerances and add complexity to their interpretation models until agreement is reached.
assertions.certainty_reason: A review author's statement with no measurement given in the paper at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that further development of tools to aid designers is needed, and that pedagogical reference materials and dedicated courses on device design are needed.
quotes: There is need for further development of tools to aid designers.
There is a need for pedagogical reference materials, including textbooks, practical tutorials, and interactive demonstrations, and for dedicated courses on device design.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's assessment of the field's gaps, not a result.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is a needs assessment as of the paper's date (v5, 30 May 2025) and may date quickly.

papers.title_in_file: Solving The Vehicle Routing Problem via Quantum Support Vector Machines
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, the encoding results text, the Inferences from Simulation section and the Conclusion; the figures and tables were not read.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study that solves 3-city and 4-city vehicle routing problems with a quantum support vector machine and a variational quantum eigensolver, comparing four encodings and three optimizers.

assertions.value: The authors report that they implemented and tested hybrid quantum machine learning methods for VRP of 3 and 4-city scenarios on 6 and 12 qubit circuits, and that the experiments ran on simulators.
quotes: In this paper, we implement and test hybrid quantum machine learning methods for solving VRP of 3 and 4-city scenarios, which use 6 and 12 qubit circuits, respectively.
providing open access to their simulators for running quantum circuits and performing the experiments reported here
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its setup, Abstract and Acknowledgment.

assertions.value: The authors report that amplitude encoding reached a nearly perfect accuracy rate (100%) and a very low error rate (0%) for 50-iteration fixed Hamiltonian simulations, and that they could simulate no more than six qubits with it because of its circuit complexity.
quotes: AE has a high, nearly perfect accuracy rate (100%) and a very low error rate (0%) for 50-iteration fixed Hamiltonian simulations.
We can simulate no more than six qubit computations due to this complexity.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Here accuracy means the run reached the classical minimum, so it is not a classification accuracy; the 100% is on a 3-city (6 qubit) case only.

assertions.value: The authors report a trend that accuracy decreases as the number of circuit layers increases, and state that over-optimization reduces accuracy rates in every scenario of their investigation.
quotes: We also observe a distinct trend that as the number of layers increases, the accuracy decreases
In every scenario of our investigation, it is evident that over-optimization reduces accuracy rates.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method outperforms the conventional method of resolving VRP via multiple optimization phases involving only VQE and QAOA.
quotes: The method not only resolves VRP, but also outperforms the conventional method of resolving VRP via multiple Optimization phases involving only VQE and QAOA.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim in the conclusion.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is with other quantum variational routes, not with a classical VRP solver; the conclusion does not show a classical baseline.

papers.title_in_file: Demonstration of a bosonic quantum classifier with data re-uploading
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, the experiment results and the Conclusion; the derivation of the theory was skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A proof-of-principle experiment that runs a data re-uploading classifier on a silicon photonic circuit with two photons.

assertions.value: The authors report a classification with a reproduction rate of approximately 94% in the proof of principle experiment, using part of the implemented optical quantum circuit with uncorrelated two-photons.
quotes: Learning and classification using part of the implemented optical quantum circuit with uncorrelated two-photons resulted in a classification with a reproduction rate of approximately 94% in the proof of principle experiment.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.

assertions.value: The authors report that 200 training data trained the optical quantum circuit, that classification was performed on 1500 test data with a correct response rate of approximately 94%, that the number of classes is 2, and that the circuit has about 220 optical components.
quotes: 200 training data were used to train the optical quantum circuit and performing classification on 1500 test data, the quantum classifier was implemented with a correct response rate of approximately 94%.
the number of classes is 2
a total of about 220 optical components on a silicon optical waveguide
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Conclusion p.6.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum states used are not entangled and that classifiers using entangled states are left for future work on the same circuit.
quotes: Although the quantum states used in this study are not entangled, research on quantum classifiers using quantum entangled states is a subject for future work possible on the same circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its demonstration, Conclusion p.6.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid quantum learning with data re-uploading on a small-scale superconducting quantum simulator
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2305.02956v2 dated 11 Jan 2024; the file name says 2023.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction and Conclusion; the experiment description and appendices were searched but not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental study of a hybrid data re-uploading classifier on a four-transmon superconducting device, with MNIST digit recognition.

assertions.value: The authors report classification accuracy around 95% on simple binary and multi-label tasks, and around 90% for a hybrid quantum model with data re-uploading when recognizing handwritten decimal digits.
quotes: We train a quantum circuit on simple binary and multi-label tasks, achieving classification accuracy around 95%, and a hybrid quantum model with data re-uploading with accuracy around 90% when recognizing handwritten decimal digits.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hardware was a linear array of four superconducting transmon artificial atoms and that the algorithm requires measurement of only one qubit.
quotes: a linear array of four superconducting transmon artificial atoms
requires measurement of only one qubit
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its hardware setup, Abstract p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the presented model does not yet outperform even the simplest classical model, such as a linear classifier, which achieves an accuracy of 95% with only 570 trainable parameters.
quotes: We note that the presented model does not yet outperform even the simplest classical model, such as linear classifier, which achieves an accuracy of 95% with only 570 trainable parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its result, Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the training process is currently orders of magnitude slower than for the classical machine learning methods.
quotes: the training process is currently orders of magnitude slower than for the classical machine learning methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its approach, Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: TOPOLOGICAL DATA ANALYSIS ON NOISY QUANTUM COMPUTERS
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2209.09371v4 (ICLR 2024). Its title is the one the record names; the file name carries the earlier v1 title (Exponential advantage on noisy quantum computers). Same paper.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, the main-result text after Theorem 1, the noisy-simulation results and the Conclusions; the appendices and proofs were not read.
papers.what_it_is: A quantum algorithm (NISQ-TDA) for estimating Betti numbers with short circuits, with a speedup analysis and noisy simulations on small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that they present NISQ-TDA, a fully implemented end-to-end quantum machine learning algorithm needing only a short circuit-depth, applicable to high-dimensional classical data, with provable asymptotic speedup for certain classes of problems.
quotes: we present NISQ-TDA, a fully implemented end-to-end quantum machine learning algorithm needing only a short circuit-depth, that is applicable to high-dimensional classical data, and with provable asymptotic speedup for certain classes of problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract-level claim by the authors; the speedup is conditional on the stated assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedup holds only for certain classes of problems, so it is not a general advantage claim.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm was successfully executed on quantum computing devices and on noisy quantum simulators, applied to small datasets, and that preliminary empirical results suggest it is robust to noise.
quotes: The algorithm was successfully executed on quantum computing devices, as well as on noisy quantum simulators, applied to small datasets.
Preliminary empirical results suggest that the algorithm is robust to noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: A preliminary empirical result on small datasets from one study.

assertions.value: The authors remark that known examples of simplicial complexes with exponentially many holes (Betti number) are limited.
quotes: We wish to remark that known examples of simplicial complexes with exponentially many holes (Betti number) are limited.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit on where its speedup applies, remark after Theorem 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that their algorithm still likely achieves exponential advantage over known classical approaches in efficiently answering whether a given simplicial complex has exponentially many holes.
quotes: More importantly, our algorithm still likely achieves exponential advantage over known classical approaches in efficiently answering the question: does the given simplicial complex have exponentially many holes or not?
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's hedged claim (likely), not a proof.

papers.title_in_file: Leveraging Analog Quantum Computing with Neutral Atoms for Solvent Configuration Prediction in Drug Discovery

assertions.value: The authors state that, as a proof of concept, both algorithms were shown to locate density maxima in non-trivial densities, and that a more simplified version was implemented on a real neutral atom QPU.
quotes: As a proof of concept, both algorithms have been shown to successfully be able to locate density maxima in non-trivial densities.
A more simplified version was implemented on a real neutral atom QPU
assertions.certainty_reason: A proof-of-concept result from one study, partly by emulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors include employees of the QPU vendor (Pasqal); the variational version was emulated, not run on hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that they limited themselves to a qubit count of 14, and that roughly 16 qubits can be emulated easily with Pulser.
quotes: Presently, we limited ourselves to a qubit count of 14.
roughly 16 qubits can be emulated easily with Pulser
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scale of its demonstration, Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that technical limitations of the present hardware prevent them from using a local Hamiltonian, which motivates the variational version using a global Rydberg Hamiltonian.
quotes: technical limitations of the present hardware prevent us from using a local Hamiltonian as in equation
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a hardware limit, Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that, thanks to the quantum nature of the algorithm, two water molecules are guaranteed never to be placed too close to each other.
quotes: We want to stress here that thanks to the quantum nature of the algorithm, two water molecules are guaranteed to never be placed too close to each other
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim of an advantage; no comparison with the classical method is given in this passage.

papers.title_in_file: The role of data embedding in equivariant quantum convolutional neural networks

assertions.value: The authors report a clear dependence of classification accuracy on the underlying embedding, especially for initial training iterations.
quotes: Our results show a clear dependence of classification accuracy on the underlying embedding, especially for initial training iterations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A numerical result from one study on a few datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the improvement in classification accuracy of EQCNN over non-equivariant QCNN may be present or absent depending on the particular embedding and dataset used.

assertions.certainty_reason: A numerical result from one study on a few datasets.
